text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said today he has yet to find a candidate to replace Muhammad Muhammad Taib who resigned as chief minister of Selangor state.
-- A national social index to gauge the success of social development programmes like new libraries, recreation facilities and training programmes will be released at the end of every year.

-- In the biggest online chat of its kind in Malaysia, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad spoke to ordinary Malaysians about the country's Multimedia Super Corridor project and how it will change their lives.
-- Contrary to market rumours, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) has not suspended any stockbroking company, a statement from the KLSE's executive chairman said.

- Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) companies have the knowledge and expertise to make it in information technology and compete in the Multimedia Super Corridor without the help of quotas, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.

-- The United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) has the final say on whether former Selangor Chief Minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib can stay on as party vice-president, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
